summary: The mail domain crate now exposes a pure sending-domain authentication admission guard that fails closed for production-active SMTP delivery unless tenant/domain isolation, non-empty normalized domain evidence, verified domain status, SPF, enforcing DMARC, and current non-future DKIM selector evidence are present.
claim_boundary: This slice is pure mail-domain policy logic only. It does not perform DNS lookup, SPF/DMARC/DKIM verification against live DNS, OpenBao key retrieval, cryptographic signing, SMTP delivery, live deliverability scoring, Gateway/TLS rollout, ArgoCD sync, remote hosted CI, or production tenant workload deployment. FD-001 product delivery remains the master-plan product goal; Oyatie Cloud is treated here as the future dogfood substrate/proof point only, not as a live substrate claim.

best_practice_research.source_quality: official RFC Editor / IETF DMARC Proposed Standard, May 2026
best_practice_research.used_for: Treat DMARC as the current domain-owner policy mechanism and avoid relying on obsoleted RFC 7489 wording for new guard semantics.

best_practice_research.source_quality: official RFC Editor / IETF SPF standard-track document
best_practice_research.used_for: Require an SPF posture signal before production-active outbound domain admission.

best_practice_research.source_quality: official RFC Editor / IETF DKIM Internet Standard
best_practice_research.used_for: Model DKIM signing-domain identity, selector/key-version provenance, and fail-closed malformed/missing signing evidence.

best_practice_research.source_quality: official RFC Editor / IETF DKIM Ed25519 update
best_practice_research.used_for: Recognize Ed25519-SHA256 as supported DKIM signing evidence while keeping RSA-SHA256 compatibility and rejecting legacy/unknown algorithms.

source_basis.use: Mail spec states every active sending domain must have DMARC policy before production activation and DKIM rotation is required.
Outbound SMTP IP requires DKIM signing, per-tenant deliverability posture, and no open relay/cross-tenant egress claims.
Threat model requires authenticated SMTP submission, DKIM signing on outbound messages, and cross-tenant sender-domain controls.
Existing mail domain crate already owns pure mail invariants and classified field conventions.

findings: Implemented the guard as a single pure function plus typed evidence/verdict structs; no adapter, DNS, crypto, or SMTP code was added.
The decision ladder is fail-closed for production-active domains and keeps quarantine/review behavior explicit for non-production modes.
The guard moves mail toward production-grade tenant-domain admission by requiring explicit evidence before a domain can be treated as production-active.

FD-001 product delivery remains the product goal; Oyatie Cloud is the hyperscaler-grade substrate intended to host these FD-001 microservices as real tenant workloads, and this guard is one domain invariant preparing mail for that dogfood path.
The slice remains honest for Oyatie Cloud dogfood: it proves domain logic only, not live DNS/OpenBao/SMTP substrate behavior.
Tests cover missing SPF, missing/enforcement-weak DMARC, missing/expired/stale DKIM, tenant/domain mismatch, unsupported DKIM algorithm, unverified domain, and redacted audit labels.
Incremental review added fail-closed handling for malformed dot-only domains after normalization and DKIM rotation timestamps that are in the future relative to the guard clock.
F3_adversarial.failing_fixture_id: cargo test -p oya-connect-mail-domain sending_domain_authentication --lib initially failed because the guard types/functions did not exist
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Removing the guard or weakening its fail-closed paths fails focused tests.

findings: Public enums name activation modes, actions, reasons, DMARC policy, and DKIM algorithms directly so future adapters can map DNS/secret-manager evidence into the guard without stringly typed seams.
Deep review for this CC-1 slice found no new runtime dependency, API ergonomics, or performance cost beyond deterministic in-memory branch checks over supplied Classified<String> inputs.
Focused and full mail-domain tests pass; cargo check, clippy -D warnings, and fmt check pass for the package.

alternatives_named: Wait for live DNS/OpenBao/SMTP adapter implementation
Add a pure domain guard now with typed evidence inputs
Add fake DNS or signing adapters for tests
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A pure guard advances production posture without inventing live infrastructure evidence or coupling domain code to adapters.
rejected_reasons: Waiting leaves a core FD-001 mail invariant unenforced in domain code.
Fake DNS/signing adapters would create false confidence and violate honest-claims discipline.

findings: No secrets or cryptographic material are handled; DKIM key data is represented only by selector/key-version/evidence references.
Tenant/domain mismatch and unsupported algorithms hard-block regardless of activation mode.
Audit labels are stable reason tokens and do not include raw domains, tenants, addresses, subjects, bodies, or URLs.
The guard is O(1) over a fixed number of small string/evidence fields and performs no I/O or allocation-heavy parsing beyond domain normalization and audit-label construction.
Deep review for this CC-1 slice found the guard performs bounded string comparisons and epoch arithmetic only; no DNS/network/crypto/SMTP I/O or unbounded scans were introduced.
SPF, DMARC, and DKIM standards are used as evidence requirements for production-active domain admission.
The guard supports DKIM rotation-age enforcement and preserves evidence references for downstream audit chains.
Reverting removes one module, one lib export, task text, evidence, and audit rows without affecting existing mailbox/message domain behavior.
Verdicts include action, reason, audit_event_label, classified tenant/domain/request IDs, and DKIM selector/key-version/evidence refs for downstream adapter logging.
Existing mail-domain APIs remain additive; no existing structs, errors, or tests were changed except module export wiring.
New identifiers use mail-domain, sending-domain, SPF/DMARC/DKIM, activation, action, and reason vocabulary from the mail spec/task evidence.
tasks/plan.md and tasks/todo.md record the slice scope, acceptance criteria, verification, and non-claims.
The new logic stays in the connect-mail domain crate and depends only on the data-boundary kernel already used by the crate.
The module is clean-architecture domain logic; live DNS, key storage, crypto signing, and SMTP delivery are left to future adapters/runtime composition.
No new dependency was added; the module reuses the existing oya-data-boundary-kernel dependency.
DKIM algorithm policy is explicit: Ed25519-SHA256 and RSA-SHA256 are accepted evidence algorithms; RSA-SHA1 and unknown algorithms reject.
No CI workflow was changed; local focused gates are recorded and full oya verify is required before submit.
